questionText:
Consider the following grammar:

$$P \rightarrow xQRS$$
$$Q \rightarrow yz \mid z$$
$$R \rightarrow w \mid \varepsilon$$
$$S \rightarrow y$$

What is $\text{FOLLOW}(Q)$?
explanation:
To find $\text{FOLLOW}(Q)$, we inspect the right-hand side of all productions to find occurrences of $Q$.

Step 1: Identify productions where $Q$ appears on the RHS
In the production rule $P \rightarrow xQRS$, $Q$ is immediately followed by $RS$.
Therefore, $\text{FOLLOW}(Q) = \text{FIRST}(RS)$.

Step 2: Calculate $\text{FIRST}(RS)$
1. $\text{FIRST}(R) = \{w, \varepsilon\}$ since $R \rightarrow w \mid \varepsilon$.
2. Since $\text{FIRST}(R)$ contains $\varepsilon$, $\text{FIRST}(RS)$ includes $(\text{FIRST}(R) \setminus \{\varepsilon\}) \cup \text{FIRST}(S)$.
3. $\text{FIRST}(S) = \{y\}$ since $S \rightarrow y$.

Combining these gives:
$$\text{FIRST}(RS) = \{w\} \cup \{y\} = \{w, y\}$$

Step 3: Conclusion
$\text{FOLLOW}(Q) = \{w, y\}$.

Hence, the correct option is C.
